records.title: Measuring blood pressure
records.summary: How to get an accurate blood pressure reading in flight.

steps: Sit restrained for 5 minutes, feet supported
Bare upper arm at heart level
Cuff 2–3 cm above the elbow crease
Take 2 readings 1 minute apart
Log the average
tips: No caffeine or exercise in the 30 minutes before
Use the same arm each time

steps: Warm the hand first
Remove nail polish or tape
Keep the hand still for 30 seconds
Read the value once it is steady
Re-check on another finger if it is low
tips: Cold fingers and movement give false low readings
Carbon monoxide gives false normal readings

steps: Wait 30 minutes after eating, drinking or exercise
Place the probe under the tongue or in the ear canal
Hold still until it signals
Log the value with the time
tips: Ear readings run slightly higher than oral

steps: Wash and dry the finger
Use the side of the fingertip
Wipe the first drop
Touch the second drop to the strip
Dispose of the lancet in the sharps box
tips: Contain blood droplets with gauze in microgravity

steps: Hold the card at arm's length
Read the smallest line with each eye
Cover one eye and look at the Amsler grid dot
Note any wavy lines or missing areas
Log No change or Something changed
tips: Same lighting and distance every day

steps: Read the active dosimeter display at the end of the day
Note the daily dose in mSv
Log it in the console
Compare with the usual rate for your location
tips: A sudden jump several times the usual rate may be a solar particle event

records.title: Building a storm shelter
records.summary: Making the most shielded space during a solar particle event.

steps: Go to the designated shelter area
Surround the crew with water bags, food and supplies
Prioritise mass on the side facing the Sun
Keep dosimeters running
Stay until mission control or the dose rate says it is safe
tips: Hydrogen-rich materials such as water and polyethylene shield best per kilogram

steps: Glove up
Stop bleeding with pressure
Irrigate with saline, capturing fluid with a towel
Close with adhesive strips, glue or stitches with local anaesthetic
Cover and check daily for infection
tips: Floating blood and fluid must be contained

records.title: Splinting a limb
records.summary: Immobilising a suspected fracture or sprain.

steps: Check pulse and feeling beyond the injury
Pad the splint
Immobilise the joints above and below the injury
Re-check pulse and feeling after splinting
tips: Do not straighten a deformed limb unless trained

records.title: CPR in microgravity
records.summary: Chest compressions when there is nothing to push against.

steps: Restrain the patient to a rigid surface
Handstand method: feet braced on the opposite wall
Or Evetts-Russomano method: legs wrapped around the patient's torso
Compress hard and fast, at least 100 per minute
Swap rescuers every 2 minutes
tips: Attach the defibrillator as soon as it arrives

records.title: Flushing the eye
records.summary: Removing debris or chemicals from the eye.

steps: Hold the eyelids open
Flush with saline from the inner corner outward
Use a towel or suction to capture the fluid
Continue for at least 15 minutes for chemicals
tips: Liquids do not run off in microgravity, so contain them

records.title: Point-of-care ultrasound
records.summary: Using the onboard ultrasound with remote guidance.

steps: Apply gel and position the probe as the reference card shows
Share the live image with the ground when the link allows
Save clips with labels
Clean the probe after use
tips: Ground experts can guide crew in real time from near-Earth locations; deeper in space, record clips for later review

records.title: Giving a medicine safely
records.summary: The five checks before any dose.

steps: Right person
Right medicine
Right dose
Right route
Right time
Record it in the console so stock and the 24-hour total update
tips: Run the dose check first: it reads current vital signs

records.title: EVA prebreathe
records.summary: Preventing decompression sickness before a spacewalk.

steps: Follow the prebreathe protocol for your suit
Breathe 100% oxygen for the required time
Light exercise if the protocol includes it
Report joint pain immediately
tips: Skipping prebreathe time raises decompression sickness risk

records.title: Preparing for landing
records.summary: Getting your body ready for gravity.

steps: Increase fluids and salt as instructed before entry
Put on compression garments
Plan to sit before standing after landing
Move your head slowly for the first days
tips: Balance and blood pressure take days to weeks to fully recover

records.title: Hygiene in a closed habitat
records.summary: Stopping germs from spreading through a small crew.

steps: Wash hands with rinseless soap before meals and after the toilet
Clean shared surfaces daily
Use separate towels
Report early symptoms of illness
tips: A closed habitat recirculates air and touches

steps: About 2 hours a day split across resistive and aerobic devices
Prioritise heavy squats and deadlifts
Add treadmill or cycle intervals
Log total minutes
tips: Missed days are the biggest risk for bone loss

records.title: Sleeping well in space
records.summary: Getting enough sleep without a normal day and night.

steps: Fixed sleep window
Use circadian lighting
Eye mask and earplugs
Secure your sleeping bag away from vents that blow on your face
tips: Exhaled CO₂ can pool around your face without airflow
